Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

everywhere adverb

also in every place, from everywhere, on all sides, here, there and everywhere

classical

Ov. Ars 3.425: cāsus ubīque valet
Quint. 10.7.27: studendum est semper et ubīque (Lewis & Short)

1ubīque: short final e (Lewis & Short ubīquē). Ov. Met. 1.214, longa mora est, quantum noxae sit ubīque repertum (quoted by Lewis & Short): the fifth foot, -bīque re-, is a dactyl. The -que is the generalising enclitic, short as in undique (Lewis & Short undĭquĕ).

ubīque1

adverb

Literally “wherever it be”, and so “everywhere”. Cicero’s phrase for “everyone everywhere” is omnēs quī ubīque sunt (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • passim — all over, here and there, in every direction

    adverb · also used · classical · Ov. F. 3.525–526: viridēs passim disjecta per herbās; Caes. BC 2.38: nūllīs ōrdinibus passim cōnsēderant (Lewis & Short)

    Scattered “hither and thither”, often “at random”, without order (Lewis & Short); see throughout.

  • undique — from everywhere; on every side

    adverb · also used · classical · Caes. BG 3.1: vīcus altissimīs montibus undique continētur (Lewis & Short); Caes. BG 1.22: ut undique ūnō tempore in hostēs impetus fieret (Lewis & Short)

    First “from all sides” (undique concurritur, people run together from everywhere, Cicero), then “on every side, all round”, and “in every respect” (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • nusquam est quī ubīque est

    he who is everywhere is nowhereSen. Ep. 2.2

  • cāsus ubīque valet; semper tibi pendeat hāmus: quō minimē crēdās gurgite, piscis erit

    chance is strong everywhere; keep your hook always hanging: in the pool where you least expect it there will be a fishOv. Ars 3.425–426

  • aut Epicūrus, quid sit voluptās, aut omnēs mortālēs quī ubīque sunt nesciunt

    either Epicurus does not know what pleasure is, or all mortals everywhere do notCic. Fin. 2.6 (Lewis & Short)

  • vīcus altissimīs montibus undique continētur

    the village is shut in on every side by very high mountainsCaes. BG 3.1 (Lewis & Short)

See also throughout, anywhere, somewhere, around.
